title: Real Estate Hoarding Design: 12 Ideas, What to Put On It and RERA Rules

faqs.question: What should a real estate hoarding include?
faqs.answer: Five things: one headline of about six or seven words, one strong image, the project name and logo, one call to action such as a large WhatsApp number or short web address, and the RERA registration number with the authority website. Everything else belongs on the project page and brochure.

faqs.question: How many words should a hoarding have?
faqs.answer: As few as possible. A common rule of thumb for outdoor ads is about seven words for the headline, because drivers see the board for only a few seconds.

faqs.question: Is the RERA number mandatory on a property hoarding?
faqs.answer: Yes. Section 11(2) of the RERA Act, 2016 says every advertisement by a promoter must prominently mention the RERA authority's website address and include the project's registration number. A hoarding is an advertisement, so the number must be on it and readable.

faqs.question: What are the common types of real estate hoarding?
faqs.answer: Roadside hoardings and billboards, unipoles at junctions, site hoardings on the boundary wall, directional boards that guide visitors to the site, wall branding in nearby localities, and panels at bus shelters, metro stations and malls.

faqs.question: Should I put a QR code on a hoarding?
faqs.answer: Only where people stand still, such as bus shelters, metro stations and mall panels, or where your state RERA authority requires one. On a roadside board seen from a moving car, a large WhatsApp number or short web address works better.

faqs.question: How do I know which hoarding brings leads?
faqs.answer: Give each board its own way to respond: a separate WhatsApp number or pre-filled message, or a tagged short link or QR code. Then compare enquiries and site visits per board after a month and move budget to the locations that work.

faqs.question: Do hoardings need permission?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Outdoor advertising normally needs permission from the local body, such as the municipal corporation or development authority, under its advertising rules. Media owners who rent sites usually handle it, but check it is in place, including for hoardings on your own boundary wall.

faqs.question: What are the most common hoarding design mistakes?
faqs.answer: Too many words, an unreadable RERA number, several phone numbers, a render that does not match the site, no way to track enquiries per board, and old launch boards left up long after the offer has ended.
